title: Create a simple calculator in ./calculator: implement
description: Create a simple calculator in ./calculator: implement add/subtract/multiply/divide in calc.py, add tests in test_calc.py using assert, add README.md. Keep isolated.
summary: I'll review the worktree changes. The calculator package is complete and isolated under `calculator/`, with `calc.py` exposing `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, and `divide` (the latter raising `ZeroDivisionError("cannot divide by zero")` instead of returning a sentinel), `test_calc.py` providing assert-based coverage of all four operations plus the zero-division case, and `README.md` documenting usage, the function reference, and how to run the tests. The implementation is dependency-free and stdlib-only, with no changes outside the new directory. Verification was by reading the sources and confirming the test suite's five test functions match the behaviors documented in the README (`5 passed, 0 failed` at exit status 0 per the documented runner); the suite was not executed in this step.

stepReports.summary: Preflight confirmed the worktree root has README.md, docs/, and .gitignore, with no calculator directory present. python3 reports 3.14.2, and no root-level package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, pytest.ini, or conftest.py exists, so verification is Python-only. Working tree was clean before changes.

Created calculator/calc.py with four typed, side-effect-free functions: add, subtract, multiply, and divide. divide raises ZeroDivisionError("cannot divide by zero") for a zero divisor. Ad-hoc check printed the expected "5 2 12 5.0".

Created calculator/test_calc.py using plain assert statements (no unittest/pytest dependency) with a sys.path fallback so it imports calc from any working directory. Includes a __main__ runner printing PASS/FAIL per test and a "N passed, M failed" summary with non-zero exit on failure. All 5 tests pass from both the repo root and the calculator directory.

Created calculator/README.md with title/description, a Python-3-only requirements line, usage snippet, a per-function reference table, the explicit ZeroDivisionError note, exact test commands for both working directories, and the directory layout. No install or pytest requirement is claimed.

All verification checks passed: python3 -m compileall -q calculator exited 0 with no output, the test runner printed "5 passed, 0 failed" and exited 0 from both the repo root and the calculator directory, the zero-division spot check printed "ok cannot divide by zero", and a deliberately wrong assertion exited non-zero proving the runner fails loudly. The generated __pycache__ was removed so git status --porcelain shows only the three intended new files.

Confirmed calculator/README.md matches the shipped behavior (function names, signatures, zero-division error and message, exact test commands, "5 passed, 0 failed" summary) and saved its full text as the task document with key "docs". Root README.md, docs/, and .gitignore are untouched; git ls-files shows only the three new calculator files and the working tree is clean.
